Prompt-level intervention (schema-informed prompting) reduces violations by ~62% but cannot eliminate them — certain relation types retain 25-30% violation rates even with explicit constraint descriptions. OntoCoDec provides **near-complete elimination (DR 15.4%→0.93%, ↓94%) at zero or positive F1 impact** through automatic ontology-to-decoder constraint compilation with two complementary layers.\\n\\n**Phase 2 confirmed (D012 bootstrap CI)**: Grammar+Semantic dual-layer constrained decoding reduces domain/range violations by 94%, eliminates entity-type and relation-vocabulary violations entirely (→0%). F1 impact is **dataset-dependent**: SciERC F1-neutral (+0.13pp, p=0.58, 95% CI [-0.24, +0.58]); DocRED F1 **significantly improved** (+0.50pp, p<0.001, 95% CI [+0.23, +0.81]). Mechanism: grammar 消除 OOV relation names (DocRED RV 29.66%→0.03%)，all_set F1 方法下 OOV=FP → fewer FP → higher precision。SciERC baseline RV 仅 1.39%，效果不显著。\\n\\n## Core Claims\\n\\n### Claim 1 (Empirical): Violation Landscape\\nLLM-based IE systems violate ontology type constraints at non-trivial rates (15.4% per-triple on SciERC, 18.7% on DocRED). Violations are **not uniformly distributed** — they concentrate on relation types with tight domain/range constraints (Feature-of 33.5%, Compare 42.4%) while loose-constraint relations show near-zero violation (Used-for 0.8%).\\n\\n**Key insight**: Violation rate is driven by **constraint tightness**, not ontology size. A small ontology with tight constraints can produce more violations than a large ontology with loose constraints.\\n\\n**Evidence**: SciERC (7 relations) 15.4%; DocRED (96 relations) 18.7% — comparable rates despite 14× ontology size difference. Schema-informed prompt on DocRED only achieves DR↓32% (vs SciERC ↓62%), confirming **prompt-level intervention scales poorly with ontology complexity**.\\n\\n### Claim 2 (Empirical): Prompt Insufficiency\\nSchema-informed prompting (explicitly describing domain/range constraints in the prompt) reduces but does not eliminate violations:\\n- Overall: 15.4% → 5.78% (-62.4%), still above 5%\\n- Per-relation: Compare 42.4% → 27.6%, Evaluate-for 24.1% → 29.9% (**worse**)\\n- Prompt intervention is unreliable at the per-relation level — some relations improve, one regresses\\n\\n**Narrative**: This is NOT about \\\"5.78% barely above 5%\\\". The story is: **prompt-level intervention is fundamentally unreliable as a guarantee mechanism**. It works statistically but cannot provide per-instance compliance. Three specific relation types retain >10% violation rates with schema-informed prompts. For safety-critical IE (biomedical, legal, regulatory), statistical reduction is insufficient — guaranteed compliance is required.\\n\\n### Claim 3 (Methodological): Composable Constraint Framework\\nOntoCoDec automatically compiles IE ontology schemas into two composable constraint layers:\\n1. **Grammar layer** (XGrammar): JSON structure + type vocabulary constraints (CFG-expressible)\\n2. **Semantic layer** (TypeConstraintProcessor): Cross-field domain/range constraints via stateful entity registry + dynamic logit masking\\n\\nThe two layers are **complementary with enabling dependency**: grammar ensures every generated relation type is in the valid vocabulary, which enables the semantic layer to look up and enforce domain/range rules for that type. Without grammar, the semantic layer encounters unknown relation types and cannot enforce constraints (explaining why semantic_only achieves only ↓24% vs full_s1 ↓94%). This is NOT \\\"synergistic\\\" (mutual amplification) — grammar is a prerequisite for semantic, not vice versa.\\n\\nThe two layers compose via bitwise AND of token masks. Recommended framing: \\\"Grammar and semantic constraints compose via bitwise AND with an enabling dependency: grammar ensures structural validity, enabling semantic constraints to enforce domain/range rules. When constraint tightness creates empty intersection between layers, the system degrades gracefully to grammar-only constraints, maintaining structural validity as a guaranteed floor.\\\"\\n\\n**Graceful degradation + Fallback 频率量化** (D008 + Reviewer 发现):\\nWhen $M_{semantic} \\\\cap M_{grammar} = \\\\emptyset$, the system falls back to grammar-only control.\\n\\n**关键量化数据（Reviewer 从日志挖掘）**:\\n- Llama DocRED full_s1: **32,921 次 fallback / 577 docs = ~57 次/doc**\\n- Llama SciERC full_s1: **5,882 次 fallback / 550 docs = ~10.7 次/doc**\\n- DocRED fallback 频率是 SciERC 的 **5.3×**\\n- Qwen DocRED fallback 率未知（日志当时无 fallback logging，需估算）\\n\\n**这直接解释了 DocRED DR 残余 10.19% vs SciERC 0.93%**: 更多 token 位置退化为 grammar-only → grammar-only 的 DR 已知为 26.17% → 高 fallback = 高残余 DR。\\n\\n**论文建议**: 在 §5 tightness 段报告 fallback 率，定义 \\\"Constraint Coverage\\\" 指标（semantic masking 实际生效的 token 比例）。这把 \\\"10.19% DR 残余\\\" 从弱点变成可量化分析的 finding。Frame as \\\"engineering robustness\\\" in §4; fallback 频率 + tightness 作为 §5 定量分析。\\n\\n**Decidability taxonomy**: Constraints classified by prefix-decidability:\\n- (a) Purely local: entity type ∈ vocabulary (grammar layer)\\n- (b) Prefix-decidable with state: relation argument types compatible with domain/range (semantic layer, requires entity registry)\\n- (c) Truly non-local: forward coreference — out of scope for forward-only decoding\\n\\n### Claim 4 (Methodological): S1 vs S2 Decoding Strategies — Architectural Ablation\\n- S1 (single-pass): Both layers applied throughout generation. **Recommended primary strategy** — simpler, slightly better metrics across the board.\\n- S2 (two-pass): Pass 1 extracts entities (grammar-only), Pass 2 generates relations with input-dependent grammar compiled from Pass 1 entities.\\n\\n**S2 full results (551/551 SciERC)**: DR 0.97% (vs S1 0.93%), CF 8.03% (vs S1 9.9%), R-F1 8.03% (vs S1 8.36%). S2 does NOT solve CF — the 1.87pp reduction is not significant. S2 also slightly worse on DR and F1. **S2 is an architectural variant demonstrating framework flexibility, not a CF solution.** Position in paper as ablation (Section 5 or Appendix), not as a core contribution.\\n\\n⚠️ **Do NOT cite pilot50 DR=0% as S2 evidence** — small-sample artifact; full run shows DR=0.97%. Per-relation S2 DR is worse than S1 on Compare (4.6% vs 2.82%), Part-of (1.25% vs 0%), Used-for (0.12% vs 0%).\\n\\n## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns\\n\\n### C1: \\\"5.78% is barely above 5% — threshold is arbitrary\\\"\\n**Response**: Don't argue about the threshold. Argue about per-relation distribution: Compare (27.6%), Evaluate-for (29.9%), Feature-of (11.3%) have double-digit violation rates with schema-informed prompt. The value proposition is per-relation guaranteed compliance, not overall statistical rate.\\n\\n### C2: \\\"Why not just post-hoc filter?\\\"\\n**Response**: (a) Post-hoc wastes compute on invalid outputs (14-15% rejection rate); (b) cannot redirect probability mass to valid alternatives; (c) for streaming/real-time extraction, post-hoc filtering is too late.\\n\\n**D010 补充：Post-hoc filtering baseline 将作为实验运行。**\\n⚠️ 风险：R-F1 仅 ~8%，DR-violating triples 多为 FP。Post-hoc 删除后 F1 可能不降（因移除的恰好是 FP）。\\n**双 framing 策略**:\\n- 如 post-hoc F1 下降 → 直接论证 \\\"重定向 > 删除\\\"\\n- 如 post-hoc F1 不降 → 报告 output coverage 差异（post-hoc 丢 15% triple slots = 信息损失）+ 3 个 post-hoc 不可替代的劣势：(1) 需后处理管线，(2) 丢弃 triple slots 不可修复，(3) 不适用流式。额外对比 per-relation recall 变化。\\n\\n### C3: \\\"Bitwise AND of two masks is not novel\\\"\\n**Response**: The novelty is not the AND operation — it's (a) the automatic compilation from ontology definitions (zero-code schema compliance), (b) the stateful entity registry enabling cross-field constraints during autoregressive generation, (c) the decidability taxonomy providing theoretical guidance, and (d) the systematic violation landscape measurement motivating the approach.\\n\\n### C4: \\\"Evaluate-for violation rate increases with schema-informed prompt\\\"\\n**Response (prior-constraint conflict framework)**: Evaluate-for has 23/36 valid pairs; Method→Task is invalid for Evaluate-for but natural in the LLM's distributional prior (\\\"Method X evaluates for Task Y\\\" is semantically plausible). Schema-informed prompting creates a **prior-constraint conflict**: the model learns to avoid Method→Task for Evaluate-for (reducing count 133→87, -34.6%), but the remaining instances are harder boundary cases where the model's type assignment strategy becomes less stable. This is not just \\\"harder instances\\\" — it's an active interference between prompt-level constraint signals and the model's learned type associations.\\n\\n**This strengthens the paper's claim**: prompt-level intervention is not merely insufficient but potentially **counterproductive** for specific constraint configurations. Decoding-time enforcement avoids this issue entirely — it operates on logits, not on the model's reasoning process, so there is no prior-constraint conflict.\\n\\n### C5: \\\"Only tested on one model (Qwen3-8B)\\\"\\n**Response**: Cross-model validation DONE. Llama-3.1-8B 零代码修改：\\n- SciERC: DR 13.34%→0.08% (↓99.4%), F1-neutral (-0.14pp)\\n- DocRED: running (预计 May 15 完成)\\n两个模型 + 两个数据集 = 4-cell 矩阵。Grammar ET/RV→0% 在两个模型上完美泛化。Constraint compiler 是 model-agnostic：只有 tokenizer mapping 是 model-specific。\\n\\n### C6: \\\"Constrained decoding degrades generation quality (CRANE, Structure Snowballing)\\\"\\n**Response**: OntoCoDec's semantic constraints are narrower than full grammar constraints — only type tokens are masked, free text is unconstrained. **D012 Bootstrap CI (10000×) 结果**:\\n- SciERC: S1 R-F1 +0.13pp, p=0.58, 95% CI [-0.24, +0.58] → F1-neutral\\n- DocRED: S1 R-F1 +0.50pp, p<0.001, 95% CI [+0.23, +0.81] → **显著提升**\\n- 机制：grammar 消除 OOV relation names → all_set 方法下减少 FP → precision 提升。DocRED RV baseline 29.66% 远高于 SciERC 1.39%，故效果在 DocRED 上显著。\\nFrame as: \\\"Constraint enforcement preserves or improves extraction quality: F1-neutral on SciERC (p=0.58); statistically significant improvement on DocRED (+0.50pp, p<0.001).\\\" 不升级为 core claim，但如实报告 significance。Note: S2 shows marginally lower F1 and fewer triples (1644 vs 1729) — two-pass does not improve quality.\\n\\n### C7: \\\"Your method trades DR violations for CF violations (cross-field consistency)\\\"\\n**Response**: Both S1 and S2 show elevated CF (per-triple rate ~8-10%). This is an inherent limitation of per-relation independent type enforcement. Must be proactively reported as a limitation. Defense:\\n\\n**CF 子类型分析（根因已确认）**：\\n- **EVR（entity-vs-relation type drift）**: 占 CF 的 >90%。同一 entity 在 entity list 和 relation triple 中被赋予不同 type。S1: 245 entities (7.34%), S2: 178 entities (5.54%, -27%)\\n- **Within-rel（同 entity 跨 relation type 不一致）**: S1: 10 (0.36%), S2: 18 (0.72%)\\n- S2 减少 EVR 但增加 within-rel——trade-off 更复杂，不是单纯好/差\\n\\n**Top 冲突模式**: Generic↔OtherScientificTerm (60次), Material↔OtherScientificTerm (28次), Material↔Method (20次)。**这些是 SciERC type system 固有的语义边界模糊区**——同一术语在不同学术语境下确实可以被合理归类为不同 type。CF 在相当程度上是 type system 模糊性的体现，非纯粹的方法缺陷。\\n\\n**论证层次**：\\n1. DR violations = structurally invalid triples（下游系统不可用）→ hard constraint\\n2. CF violations = same entity gets different types across relations → individual triples remain type-valid, only cross-triple consistency broken → soft preference\\n3. CF 的根因是 type system 语义边界模糊 + per-relation 独立 enforcement，非 bug\\n4. Future work: cross-relation global consistency pass (entity-level type consensus before relation-specific enforcement)\\n\\n**机制归因（口径对账确认）**：grammar_only CF=0.08%（与 unconstrained 持平），full_s1 CF=9.90%，full_s2 CF=8.03%。**CF 100% 由 semantic 层引入，grammar 层无贡献。** 这为 \\\"CF 是 semantic type enforcement 的系统性副作用\\\" 提供干净的消融证据。\\n\\n**论文数字口径**：CF rate 用 violation_checker 口径（denominator=total_entities，与 DR/RV/ET 一致）。分析段落额外给 entity-level EVR 率 + 受影响样本比例。注意：analyze_cf 脚本的 EVR/WR 两维度不是独立的（WR⊂EVR），论文中不要作为两个独立维度报告。\\n\\n**Do NOT hide this data.** Proactive disclosure + severity distinction + root cause analysis\\n\\n... ## Target Venue
EMNLP 2026 (ARR submission May 25, 2026)

## Title
OntoCoDec: Near-Complete Type-Valid Information Extraction via Compiled Ontology Constraints
(Note: "Guaranteed" dropped per Reviewer — S1 DR=0.93%, S2 DR=0.97%, neither achieves 0%. "Near-Complete" is honest and defensible.)

## Core Insight
LLM-based IE systems produce systematic ontology constraint violations concentrated in specific relation types. Prompt-level intervention (schema-informed prompting) reduces violations by ~62% but cannot eliminate them — certain relation types retain 25-30% violation rates even with explicit constraint descriptions. OntoCoDec provides **near-complete elimination (DR 15.4%→0.93%, ↓94%) at zero or positive F1 impact** through automatic ontology-to-decoder constraint compilation with two complementary layers.

**Phase 2 confirmed (D012 bootstrap CI)**: Grammar+Semantic dual-layer constrained decoding reduces domain/range violations by 94%, eliminates entity-type and relation-vocabulary violations entirely (→0%). F1 impact is **dataset-dependent**: SciERC F1-neutral (+0.13pp, p=0.58, 95% CI [-0.24, +0.58]); DocRED F1 **significantly improved** (+0.50pp, p<0.001, 95% CI [+0.23, +0.81]). Mechanism: grammar 消除 OOV relation names (DocRED RV 29.66%→0.03%)，all_set F1 方法下 OOV=FP → fewer FP → higher precision。SciERC baseline RV 仅 1.39%，效果不显著。

## Core Claims

### Claim 1 (Empirical): Violation Landscape
LLM-based IE systems violate ontology type constraints at non-trivial rates (15.4% per-triple on SciERC, 18.7% on DocRED). Violations are **not uniformly distributed** — they concentrate on relation types with tight domain/range constraints (Feature-of 33.5%, Compare 42.4%) while loose-constraint relations show near-zero violation (Used-for 0.8%).

**Key insight**: Violation rate is driven by **constraint tightness**, not ontology size. A small ontology with tight constraints can produce more violations than a large ontology with loose constraints.

**Evidence**: SciERC (7 relations) 15.4%; DocRED (96 relations) 18.7% — comparable rates despite 14× ontology size difference. Schema-informed prompt on DocRED only achieves DR↓32% (vs SciERC ↓62%), confirming **prompt-level intervention scales poorly with ontology complexity**.

### Claim 2 (Empirical): Prompt Insufficiency
Schema-informed prompting (explicitly describing domain/range constraints in the prompt) reduces but does not eliminate violations:
- Overall: 15.4% → 5.78% (-62.4%), still above 5%
- Per-relation: Compare 42.4% → 27.6%, Evaluate-for 24.1% → 29.9% (**worse**)
- Prompt intervention is unreliable at the per-relation level — some relations improve, one regresses

**Narrative**: This is NOT about "5.78% barely above 5%". The story is: **prompt-level intervention is fundamentally unreliable as a guarantee mechanism**. It works statistically but cannot provide per-instance compliance. Three specific relation types retain >10% violation rates with schema-informed prompts. For safety-critical IE (biomedical, legal, regulatory), statistical reduction is insufficient — guaranteed compliance is required.

### Claim 3 (Methodological): Composable Constraint Framework
OntoCoDec automatically compiles IE ontology schemas into two composable constraint layers:
1. **Grammar layer** (XGrammar): JSON structure + type vocabulary constraints (CFG-expressible)
2. **Semantic layer** (TypeConstraintProcessor): Cross-field domain/range constraints via stateful entity registry + dynamic logit masking

The two layers are **complementary with enabling dependency**: grammar ensures every generated relation type is in the valid vocabulary, which enables the semantic layer to look up and enforce domain/range rules for that type. Without grammar, the semantic layer encounters unknown relation types and cannot enforce constraints (explaining why semantic_only achieves only ↓24% vs full_s1 ↓94%). This is NOT "synergistic" (mutual amplification) — grammar is a prerequisite for semantic, not vice versa.

The two layers compose via bitwise AND of token masks. Recommended framing: "Grammar and semantic constraints compose via bitwise AND with an enabling dependency: grammar ensures structural validity, enabling semantic constraints to enforce domain/range rules. When constraint tightness creates empty intersection between layers, the system degrades gracefully to grammar-only constraints, maintaining structural validity as a guaranteed floor."

**Graceful degradation + Fallback 频率量化** (D008 + Reviewer 发现):
When $M_{semantic} \cap M_{grammar} = \emptyset$, the system falls back to grammar-only control.

**关键量化数据（Reviewer 从日志挖掘）**:
- Llama DocRED full_s1: **32,921 次 fallback / 577 docs = ~57 次/doc**
- Llama SciERC full_s1: **5,882 次 fallback / 550 docs = ~10.7 次/doc**
- DocRED fallback 频率是 SciERC 的 **5.3×**
- Qwen DocRED fallback 率未知（日志当时无 fallback logging，需估算）

**这直接解释了 DocRED DR 残余 10.19% vs SciERC 0.93%**: 更多 token 位置退化为 grammar-only → grammar-only 的 DR 已知为 26.17% → 高 fallback = 高残余 DR。

**论文建议**: 在 §5 tightness 段报告 fallback 率，定义 "Constraint Coverage" 指标（semantic masking 实际生效的 token 比例）。这把 "10.19% DR 残余" 从弱点变成可量化分析的 finding。Frame as "engineering robustness" in §4; fallback 频率 + tightness 作为 §5 定量分析。

**Decidability taxonomy**: Constraints classified by prefix-decidability:
- (a) Purely local: entity type ∈ vocabulary (grammar layer)
- (b) Prefix-decidable with state: relation argument types compatible with domain/range (semantic layer, requires entity registry)
- (c) Truly non-local: forward coreference — out of scope for forward-only decoding

### Claim 4 (Methodological): S1 vs S2 Decoding Strategies — Architectural Ablation
- S1 (single-pass): Both layers applied throughout generation. **Recommended primary strategy** — simpler, slightly better metrics across the board.
- S2 (two-pass): Pass 1 extracts entities (grammar-only), Pass 2 generates relations with input-dependent grammar compiled from Pass 1 entities.

**S2 full results (551/551 SciERC)**: DR 0.97% (vs S1 0.93%), CF 8.03% (vs S1 9.9%), R-F1 8.03% (vs S1 8.36%). S2 does NOT solve CF — the 1.87pp reduction is not significant. S2 also slightly worse on DR and F1. **S2 is an architectural variant demonstrating framework flexibility, not a CF solution.** Position in paper as ablation (Section 5 or Appendix), not as a core contribution.

⚠️ **Do NOT cite pilot50 DR=0% as S2 evidence** — small-sample artifact; full run shows DR=0.97%. Per-relation S2 DR is worse than S1 on Compare (4.6% vs 2.82%), Part-of (1.25% vs 0%), Used-for (0.12% vs 0%).

## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns

### C1: "5.78% is barely above 5% — threshold is arbitrary"
**Response**: Don't argue about the threshold. Argue about per-relation distribution: Compare (27.6%), Evaluate-for (29.9%), Feature-of (11.3%) have double-digit violation rates with schema-informed prompt. The value proposition is per-relation guaranteed compliance, not overall statistical rate.

### C2: "Why not just post-hoc filter?"
**Response**: (a) Post-hoc wastes compute on invalid outputs (14-15% rejection rate); (b) cannot redirect probability mass to valid alternatives; (c) for streaming/real-time extraction, post-hoc filtering is too late.

**D010 补充：Post-hoc filtering baseline 将作为实验运行。**
⚠️ 风险：R-F1 仅 ~8%，DR-violating triples 多为 FP。Post-hoc 删除后 F1 可能不降（因移除的恰好是 FP）。
**双 framing 策略**:
- 如 post-hoc F1 下降 → 直接论证 "重定向 > 删除"
- 如 post-hoc F1 不降 → 报告 output coverage 差异（post-hoc 丢 15% triple slots = 信息损失）+ 3 个 post-hoc 不可替代的劣势：(1) 需后处理管线，(2) 丢弃 triple slots 不可修复，(3) 不适用流式。额外对比 per-relation recall 变化。

### C3: "Bitwise AND of two masks is not novel"
**Response**: The novelty is not the AND operation — it's (a) the automatic compilation from ontology definitions (zero-code schema compliance), (b) the stateful entity registry enabling cross-field constraints during autoregressive generation, (c) the decidability taxonomy providing theoretical guidance, and (d) the systematic violation landscape measurement motivating the approach.

### C4: "Evaluate-for violation rate increases with schema-informed prompt"
**Response (prior-constraint conflict framework)**: Evaluate-for has 23/36 valid pairs; Method→Task is invalid for Evaluate-for but natural in the LLM's distributional prior ("Method X evaluates for Task Y" is semantically plausible). Schema-informed prompting creates a **prior-constraint conflict**: the model learns to avoid Method→Task for Evaluate-for (reducing count 133→87, -34.6%), but the remaining instances are harder boundary cases where the model's type assignment strategy becomes less stable. This is not just "harder instances" — it's an active interference between prompt-level constraint signals and the model's learned type associations.

**This strengthens the paper's claim**: prompt-level intervention is not merely insufficient but potentially **counterproductive** for specific constraint configurations. Decoding-time enforcement avoids this issue entirely — it operates on logits, not on the model's reasoning process, so there is no prior-constraint conflict.

### C5: "Only tested on one model (Qwen3-8B)"
**Response**: Cross-model validation DONE. Llama-3.1-8B 零代码修改：
- SciERC: DR 13.34%→0.08% (↓99.4%), F1-neutral (-0.14pp)
- DocRED: running (预计 May 15 完成)
两个模型 + 两个数据集 = 4-cell 矩阵。Grammar ET/RV→0% 在两个模型上完美泛化。Constraint compiler 是 model-agnostic：只有 tokenizer mapping 是 model-specific。

### C6: "Constrained decoding degrades generation quality (CRANE, Structure Snowballing)"
**Response**: OntoCoDec's semantic constraints are narrower than full grammar constraints — only type tokens are masked, free text is unconstrained. **D012 Bootstrap CI (10000×) 结果**:
- SciERC: S1 R-F1 +0.13pp, p=0.58, 95% CI [-0.24, +0.58] → F1-neutral
- DocRED: S1 R-F1 +0.50pp, p<0.001, 95% CI [+0.23, +0.81] → **显著提升**
- 机制：grammar 消除 OOV relation names → all_set 方法下减少 FP → precision 提升。DocRED RV baseline 29.66% 远高于 SciERC 1.39%，故效果在 DocRED 上显著。
Frame as: "Constraint enforcement preserves or improves extraction quality: F1-neutral on SciERC (p=0.58); statistically significant improvement on DocRED (+0.50pp, p<0.001)." 不升级为 core claim，但如实报告 significance。Note: S2 shows marginally lower F1 and fewer triples (1644 vs 1729) — two-pass does not improve quality.

### C7: "Your method trades DR violations for CF violations (cross-field consistency)"
**Response**: Both S1 and S2 show elevated CF (per-triple rate ~8-10%). This is an inherent limitation of per-relation independent type enforcement. Must be proactively reported as a limitation. Defense:

**CF 子类型分析（根因已确认）**：
- **EVR（entity-vs-relation type drift）**: 占 CF 的 >90%。同一 entity 在 entity list 和 relation triple 中被赋予不同 type。S1: 245 entities (7.34%), S2: 178 entities (5.54%, -27%)
- **Within-rel（同 entity 跨 relation type 不一致）**: S1: 10 (0.36%), S2: 18 (0.72%)
- S2 减少 EVR 但增加 within-rel——trade-off 更复杂，不是单纯好/差

**Top 冲突模式**: Generic↔OtherScientificTerm (60次), Material↔OtherScientificTerm (28次), Material↔Method (20次)。**这些是 SciERC type system 固有的语义边界模糊区**——同一术语在不同学术语境下确实可以被合理归类为不同 type。CF 在相当程度上是 type system 模糊性的体现，非纯粹的方法缺陷。

**论证层次**：
1. DR violations = structurally invalid triples（下游系统不可用）→ hard constraint
2. CF violations = same entity gets different types across relations → individual triples remain type-valid, only cross-triple consistency broken → soft preference
3. CF 的根因是 type system 语义边界模糊 + per-relation 独立 enforcement，非 bug
4. Future work: cross-relation global consistency pass (entity-level type consensus before relation-specific enforcement)

**机制归因（口径对账确认）**：grammar_only CF=0.08%（与 unconstrained 持平），full_s1 CF=9.90%，full_s2 CF=8.03%。**CF 100% 由 semantic 层引入，grammar 层无贡献。** 这为 "CF 是 semantic type enforcement 的系统性副作用" 提供干净的消融证据。

% Section 7 — Conclusion
% Data source: Phase 2 SciERC registry experiments + Phase 0 DocRED
% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_unconstrained, phase2_scierc_full_s1,
%          phase0_scierc_unconstrained, phase0_docred_unconstrained
% All numbers verified against registry 2026-05-14.

We presented OntoCoDec, a framework that automatically compiles IE ontology schemas into token-level decoding constraints to enforce type validity at generation time.
Our work makes three contributions.

First, we conducted the first systematic study of ontological constraint violations in LLM-based IE (\S\ref{sec:violation_landscape}).
Across two benchmarks with substantially different ontology sizes---SciERC (7~relations) and DocRED (96~relations)---we found that domain/range violation rates are comparable (15.37\% vs.\ 18.70\%), % exp_ids: phase0_scierc_unconstrained, phase0_docred_unconstrained
indicating that violation severity is driven by \emph{constraint tightness} (valid type pairs per relation) rather than ontology scale.

Second, we introduced a two-layer constraint architecture that decomposes ontological enforcement into complementary mechanisms:
a \emph{grammar layer} (XGrammar CFG) that eliminates structural violations (RV, ET\,$\to$\,0\%) and a \emph{semantic layer} (TypeConstraintProcessor with a stateful entity registry) that enforces domain/range constraints at the token level. % exp_id: phase2_scierc_grammar_only
The grammar layer serves as an enabling prerequisite for the semantic layer; the two compose via bitwise AND over candidate token sets.

Third, we validated OntoCoDec empirically.
On SciERC, the full system reduces domain/range violations from 15.37\% to 0.93\%---a 94\% relative reduction---while completely eliminating RV and ET violations, with no significant impact on relation F1 ($+$0.13 percentage points, $p > 0.05$). % exp_id: phase2_scierc_full_s1
\placeholder{DocRED DR result: unconstrained DR=18.70\% $\to$ full system DR=??\%, with RV 28.90\%$\to$??\% and ET 7.50\%$\to$??\%.}

\paragraph{Limitations.}
Several limitations qualify these findings.
The semantic layer introduces cross-field consistency (CF) violations: CF rises from 0.08\% under unconstrained decoding to 9.90\% with full constraints. % exp_ids: phase2_scierc_unconstrained, phase2_scierc_full_s1
This is a systematic consequence of per-relation independent type enforcement---when the same entity appears across multiple triples, each relation's domain/range constraint may assign it a different type, producing entity-versus-relation type drift.
The grammar layer alone does not elevate CF (0.08\%, matching the unconstrained baseline), confirming that CF is entirely attributable to the semantic layer. % exp_id: phase2_scierc_grammar_only
Resolving this cross-relation type coherence problem is an open challenge, not a trivial implementation fix.
Beyond CF, all experiments use a single model (Qwen3-8B); while the constraint compiler is model-agnostic by design, cross-model validation remains incomplete.
Results are reported on two datasets under zero-shot prompting only, and integration with fine-tuned models has not been explored.

\paragraph{Future Work.}
We identify four directions.
(1)~Cross-model validation on architectures such as Llama-3.1-8B and quantized 70B-class models to verify model-agnostic generalization.
(2)~Global entity-level type consensus during decoding---maintaining a shared entity registry across all relations within an instance---to resolve CF violations.
(3)~Integration with fine-tuned models, combining constraint-aware training objectives with decoding-time enforcement.
(4)~Extension to non-English ontologies to evaluate cross-lingual applicability.

% Discussion paragraphs for §7
% Three standalone paragraphs: (1) Low F1 practical significance,
% (2) CF severity argument, (3) F1 significance difference explanation.
% All quantitative claims traced to registry exp_ids.

%%% Paragraph 1: Low F1 Practical Significance %%%
% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_full_s1 (R-F1=8.36%), phase0_scierc_unconstrained (baseline violations)

\paragraph{Practical Significance of Zero-Shot F1.}
Our reported relation F1 of approximately 8\% reflects the inherent difficulty of zero-shot closed IE, where the model receives no task-specific training examples.
For reference, supervised state-of-the-art systems on SciERC achieve 40--50\% F1 with full training data~\citep{zhong2021frustratingly,ye2022packed}.
Constraint enforcement operates orthogonally to extraction quality: it restricts the output space to ontologically valid triples regardless of the underlying model's accuracy.
When applied to fine-tuned models that reach competitive F1 levels, the same constraints remain necessary---Phase~0 analysis confirms that even well-prompted models exhibit non-trivial violation rates (15.37\% DR on SciERC).
% exp_id: phase0_scierc_unconstrained
In our evaluation, F1 serves as a \emph{control variable} verifying that constraint enforcement does not degrade extraction quality, not as an optimization target.
The contribution of this work is the constraint enforcement method itself; the zero-shot setting isolates its effect from confounds introduced by task-specific fine-tuning.

%%% Paragraph 2: CF Severity Argument %%%
% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_full_s1 (CF=9.90%), phase2_scierc_grammar_only (CF=0.08%),
%          phase2_docred_full_s1 (CF=2.57%)

\paragraph{Severity of Cross-Field Violations.}
Domain/range (DR) violations produce structurally invalid triples---a triple asserting that a \emph{Task} entity fills the \emph{domain} slot of \textsc{Part-of}, which requires \emph{Method}, cannot be consumed by any downstream system without error.
DR violations are therefore hard constraints.
Cross-field consistency (CF) violations are qualitatively different: each individual triple remains type-valid with respect to its own relation's domain/range rules; only cross-triple consistency is broken when the same entity receives different types across relations.
The dominant conflict pattern---\emph{Generic}$\leftrightarrow$\emph{OtherScientificTerm} (60 of 245~affected entities on SciERC)---reflects genuine semantic ambiguity in the type system rather than a systematic method failure.
% exp_id: phase2_scierc_full_s1
Ablation evidence cleanly attributes CF to the semantic layer: grammar-only decoding yields CF\,=\,0.08\%, matching the unconstrained baseline, while the full system reaches 9.90\% on SciERC and 2.57\% on DocRED.
% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_grammar_only, phase2_docred_full_s1
This arises from per-relation independent enforcement, where each relation's constraint mask is computed without access to type decisions made for other relations.
A natural extension is a global entity-level type consensus pass that resolves entity types before relation-specific enforcement.

%%% Paragraph 3: F1 Significance Difference Explanation %%%
% exp_ids: d012_bootstrap_ci (DocRED +0.50pp p<0.001, SciERC +0.13pp p=0.58),
%          phase0_docred_unconstrained (RV=29.66%), phase0_scierc_unconstrained (RV=1.39%)

\paragraph{Dataset-Dependent F1 Impact.}
The divergence in F1 significance between DocRED ($+$0.50\,pp, $p < 0.001$, 95\% CI [$+$0.23, $+$0.81]) and SciERC ($+$0.13\,pp, $p = 0.58$, 95\% CI [$-$0.24, $+$0.58]) traces to a single mechanism: grammar-layer elimination of out-of-vocabulary (OOV) relation names.
% exp_id: d012_bootstrap_ci
Under the all-valid-set evaluation protocol, a predicted triple whose relation name does not appear in the ontology is counted as a false positive.
The DocRED baseline exhibits a relation-vocabulary (RV) violation rate of 29.66\%---5{,}189 predictions with OOV relation names---all of which become false positives under this protocol.
% exp_id: phase0_docred_unconstrained
The grammar layer eliminates these OOV predictions, removing a substantial source of false positives and yielding a statistically significant precision gain.
On SciERC, the baseline RV rate is only 1.39\% (24~OOV predictions), too few to produce a detectable F1 effect.

% Discussion paragraphs for §7
% Three standalone paragraphs: (1) Low F1 practical significance,
% (2) CF severity argument, (3) F1 significance difference explanation.
% All quantitative claims traced to registry exp_ids.

%%% Paragraph 1: Low F1 Practical Significance %%%
% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_full_s1 (R-F1=8.36%), phase0_scierc_unconstrained (baseline violations)

\paragraph{Practical Significance of Zero-Shot F1.}
Our reported relation F1 of approximately 8\% reflects the inherent difficulty of zero-shot closed IE, where the model receives no task-specific training examples.
For reference, supervised state-of-the-art systems on SciERC achieve 40--50\% F1 with full training data~\citep{zhong2021frustratingly,ye2022packed}.
Constraint enforcement operates orthogonally to extraction quality: it restricts the output space to ontologically valid triples regardless of the underlying model's accuracy.
When applied to fine-tuned models that reach competitive F1 levels, the same constraints remain necessary---Phase~0 analysis confirms that even well-prompted models exhibit non-trivial violation rates (15.37\% DR on SciERC).
% exp_id: phase0_scierc_unconstrained
In our evaluation, F1 serves as a \emph{control variable} verifying that constraint enforcement does not degrade extraction quality, not as an optimization target.
The contribution of this work is the constraint enforcement method itself; the zero-shot setting isolates its effect from confounds introduced by task-specific fine-tuning.

%%% Paragraph 2: CF Severity Argument %%%
% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_full_s1 (CF=9.90%), phase2_scierc_grammar_only (CF=0.08%),
%          phase2_docred_full_s1 (CF=2.57%)

\paragraph{Severity of Cross-Field Violations.}
Domain/range (DR) violations produce structurally invalid triples---a triple asserting that a \emph{Task} entity fills the \emph{domain} slot of \textsc{Part-of}, which requires \emph{Method}, cannot be consumed by any downstream system without error.
DR violations are therefore hard constraints.
Cross-field consistency (CF) violations are qualitatively different: each individual triple remains type-valid with respect to its own relation's domain/range rules; only cross-triple consistency is broken when the same entity receives different types across relations.
The dominant conflict pattern---\emph{Generic}$\leftrightarrow$\emph{OtherScientificTerm} (60 of 245~affected entities on SciERC)---reflects genuine semantic ambiguity in the type system rather than a systematic method failure.
% exp_id: phase2_scierc_full_s1
Ablation evidence cleanly attributes CF to the semantic layer: grammar-only decoding yields CF\,=\,0.08\%, matching the unconstrained baseline, while the full system reaches 9.90\% on SciERC and 2.57\% on DocRED.
% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_grammar_only, phase2_docred_full_s1
This arises from per-relation independent enforcement, where each relation's constraint mask is computed without access to type decisions made for other relations.
A natural extension is a global entity-level type consensus pass that resolves entity types before relation-specific enforcement.

%%% Paragraph 3: F1 Significance Difference Explanation %%%
% exp_ids: d012_bootstrap_ci (DocRED +0.50pp p<0.001, SciERC +0.13pp p=0.58),
%          phase0_docred_unconstrained (RV=29.66%), phase0_scierc_unconstrained (RV=1.39%)

\paragraph{Dataset-Dependent F1 Impact.}
The divergence in F1 significance between DocRED ($+$0.50\,pp, $p < 0.001$, 95\% CI [$+$0.23, $+$0.81]) and SciERC ($+$0.13\,pp, $p = 0.58$, 95\% CI [$-$0.24, $+$0.58]) traces to a single mechanism: grammar-layer elimination of out-of-vocabulary (OOV) relation names.
% exp_id: d012_bootstrap_ci
Under the all-valid-set evaluation protocol, a predicted triple whose relation name does not appear in the ontology is counted as a false positive.
The DocRED baseline exhibits a relation-vocabulary (RV) violation rate of 29.66\%---5{,}189 predictions with OOV relation names---all of which become false positives under this protocol.
% exp_id: phase0_docred_unconstrained
The grammar layer eliminates these OOV predictions, removing a substantial source of false positives and yielding a statistically significant precision gain.
On SciERC, the baseline RV rate is only 1.39\% (24~OOV predictions), too few to produce a detectable F1 effect.
% exp_id: phase0_scierc_unconstrained
The F1 improvement on DocRED is thus a direct, mechanistically transparent consequence of vocabulary enforcement at scale, not an artifact of constraint-induced distribution shift.
